images.title: Trapezium on a grid
images.purpose: Shows a trapezium on a grid split into a square and a right triangle whose areas add.
images.composition: One trapezium on a light grid, large and centred.
images.exact_structure: Plain white background, lots of empty space, the figure large and centred, thin dark outlines. Only the labels listed appear; no other text, no scenery, no characters. A faint grey (#6B7280) grid 6 squares wide and 4 squares tall. Trapezium with bottom side 6 squares long, left side vertical 4 squares tall (right angle at the bottom left corner), top side 4 squares long starting at the top left corner, and a slanting right side from the end of the top side down to the bottom right corner. A dashed dark vertical line from the right end of the top side down to the bottom side splits it into a 4 by 4 square (16 whole grid squares) filled teal (#0072B2) and a right triangle with legs 2 and 4 filled amber (#E69F00). Labels: 4 units above the top side; 6 units under the bottom side; 16 inside the square; 4 inside the triangle; below the figure 16 + 4 = 20 square units. Check: 1/2 × 2 × 4 = 4, 16 + 4 = 20.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
images.takeaway: Break the trapezium into a square and a triangle, find each area and add.
images.description: Shows a trapezium on a grid split into a square and a right triangle whose areas add.
images.context: Matches the worked example: AB = 4, DC = 6, height 4, area 20 square units.
images.teaching_notes: The triangle is half of a 2 by 4 rectangle: 8 squares halved gives 4.

image_decisions.why: Counting on a grid needs a grid picture; it shows why the cut triangle is exactly 4.
